goal: Pick up the two T-shaped blocks, exchange their positions, and set each down with the orientation the other one had, then return the arm(s) to the start pose.
instruction_templates: Pick up the two T-shaped blocks, swap their positions, and place them back with the correct orientations.
success: t0's ROOT position is within 0.02 m horizontally (XY only; z not checked) of t1's INITIAL root XY position (captured when the evaluation starts, i.e. the reset layout).
t1's ROOT position is within 0.02 m horizontally (XY only) of t0's INITIAL root XY position.
t0's orientation (full 3D quaternion) is within 3 degrees (strictly less; quaternion angular distance) of t1's INITIAL orientation.
t1's orientation is within 3 degrees of t0's INITIAL orientation.

all_robot_back_to_origin: every target arm's end-effector pose is within 0.15 m per axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angular distance) of its start-of-episode pose (the arms must be returned to roughly their starting pose).
evaluation: Success conditions form ONE stage: after every action (once all simulation sub-steps of that action are done) the reward manager evaluates all conditions; the episode succeeds as soon as ALL hold simultaneously at the same moment (reward 1 -> episode ends with success). Conditions are not latched or ordered. Otherwise the episode ends as a failure after step_lim=400 actions (the check made after the last action still counts). No early-fail rule exists apart from the environment being flagged invalid (e.g. a required label missing / physics broken).
objects: t0: rigid T-shaped block (category 't', index 0), 1 total, at Table-relative x in [-0.09,-0.03], y in [-0.2,-0.15], random yaw over the full 360 degrees
t1: rigid T-shaped block (category 't', index 1), 1 total, at x in [0.03,0.09], y in [-0.2,-0.15], random yaw over 360 degrees
needs_memory_or_language: Memory: the solver must remember (or note from the first observation) each T block's initial position and orientation, because the goals are defined relative to the INITIAL poses of the other block; once the blocks move the targets cannot be read off the scene any more.
end_requirements: All target (controlled) arms must be back near their start pose when success is evaluated (it is one of the success conditions, see success list): every target arm's end-effector position within 0.15 m on EACH of x, y, z (per-axis, not Euclidean) and orientation within 20 degrees of its pose at the start of the episode (pose recorded right after the robot is set to its initial state). Gripper opening is NOT checked by the success test.
notes: The target poses are computed once at the start (run_reward is called after reset, before any action) from the initial root poses: t0 must end at t1's start pose and t1 at t0's start pose. Orientation tolerance is only 3 degrees on the full 3D rotation (blocks must lie flat in the same way), and position tolerance 0.02 m on the root points. The two blocks start close together (root distance roughly 0.06-0.18 m along x) so one block usually has to be parked elsewhere first. t0 and t1 are different assets (index 0 vs 1) so their root frames/shapes may differ; the checks compare root frames, not shapes. No gripper-open requirement in success. Success is evaluated on object root poses/points, not on gripper contact. Object geometry sizes/asset dimensions are not in the source and cannot be determined statically.
